liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): First set opens with this song and Crazy Fingers, surprising listeners with early placement [23]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Second set starts with this track, revitalizing it from its usual lethargic late-70s style [23]
- **Dear Mr Fantasy** (1 review): Reviewers call this sequence the best version ever played, citing high energy and chills [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-07-02.138306.mtx.miller.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 159 min; rated 4.4/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1989-07-02.fob.nak300.andrewf.99912.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 158 min [3]
- **gd1989-07-02.fob.nak300.andrewf.99911.flac24**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 158 min [4]
- **gd1989-07-02.153412.MTX.photoLeon.t-flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 162 min [5]
- **gd89-07-02.nak.8243.sbefail.shnf**: source not stated; 20 songs; 165 min; rated 4.1/5 by 30 [10]. Said about its sound: Listener describes the recording quality as great for its type, closing out the summer; Recording quality is described as just okay, with the Eyes of the World section disappointing [26][32]

## Around the show

- Attendee paid ninety dollars to a ticket broker, experiencing a wild scene with colorful people [27]
- Fake mail-order tickets with multi-colored paper inside led to some fans being turned away [28]
- Miserably humid day caused heat stroke, requiring fire hoses to cool the crowd near the stage [30]
- Spectacular sunny but hot and humid day; Jerry walked to the mic to ask how everyone was doing [34]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-07-02.138306.mtx.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Ultra Matrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [1]. Also: Two sets of master were used to complete the show, with 24-bit converted to 16-bit [1]
- **gd1989-07-02.fob.nak300.andrewf.99912.flac16**: taped by Andrew F.; transferred by Andrew F.; source: FOB AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90's with no Dolby. Mics on 8-foot stand, approx 10 feet in front of SBD area and 15 feet to… [3]. Also: Patch from ID-8243 used in Drums; second set disc break is seamless [3]
- **gd1989-07-02.fob.nak300.andrewf.99911.flac24**: taped by Andrew F.; transferred by Andrew F.; source: FOB AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns FOB AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90's with no Dolby. Mics on 8-foot stand, approx 10 feet… [4]. Also: Patch from ID-8243 used in Drums; includes Sittin' On Top Of The World and This Land Is Your Land [4]
- **gd1989-07-02.153412.MTX.photoLeon.t-flac16**: source: A photoLeon Matrix [5]. Also: Matrix created by Joe Noel; source 2 pitch corrected; EotW missing vocals from 00:13 to 00:49 [5]
- **gd89-07-02.nak.8243.sbefail.shnf**: taped by Jill and Rob R; source: 3 Nak CM 300's - 2 CP 4's (Shotguns) 1 CP3 ( Super Omni ) arranged in an X-Y pattern [10]. Also: Uploader mentions a Schoeps spaced omni source, though archive.org rejected public uploads [29]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Sullivan Stadium - July 2, 1989](https://www.dead.net/show/july-2-1989) [36]
- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1989-07-02 Sullivan Stadium, Foxboro, MA](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/02/grateful-dead-1989-07-02-sullivan.html) [37]
